title.title: The prime factors of $p - 1$ behave like a random integer's
title.subtitle: Claim: for every $\delta > 0$, $x^{1-o(1)}$ primes in $(2x, 5x]$ have $p - 1$ free of primes above $x^{\delta}$

object.axisLabel: $\delta$: every prime factor of $p - 1$ is at most $x^{\delta}$

beats.text: How small can every prime factor of $p - 1$ be, for many primes $p$ up to $x$?
Before: down to $x^{0.2844}$ (Lichtman 2022), with $x/(\log x)^C$ such primes
The claim: any power $x^{\delta}$, and $p - 1$ factors like a random integer

achievement.note: Also: the factors of $p - 1$ follow the Poisson–Dirichlet law
